# The Re-Use of Non-Traditional Data for Public Interest Purposes

[A Curated Compilation of 100 Use Cases (2024-2026)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/19ojoRQgzRZk5WNxG6m62ZHEGgelbH0pqSZaxKY5pLAU/edit?pli=1&tab=t.0) by Stefaan Verhulst and Adam Zable: “The rapid digitization of society has fundamentally transformed the data landscape. Every day, billions of interactions with digital platforms, mobile devices, sensors, financial systems, satellites, connected infrastructure, and other technologies generate unprecedented volumes of information about human behavior, economic activity, environmental change, and public systems. While these data are typically created for operational, commercial, or technological purposes rather than official statistics or research, they increasingly offer valuable opportunities to address public-interest challenges when reused responsibly.

This so-called non-traditional data (NTD) has emerged as an important complement to conventional sources of evidence such as surveys, censuses, administrative records, and official statistics. It can provide information that is more timely, granular, continuous, and behaviorally rich than many traditional datasets, enabling governments, researchers, humanitarian organizations, and civil society to better understand rapidly changing conditions and respond more effectively.

From tracking disease outbreaks and population displacement to monitoring environmental degradation, estimating economic activity, improving disaster response, and informing urban planning, NTD is becoming an increasingly important part of the evidence base that supports public decision-making.

At the same time, the landscape for accessing and reusing non-traditional data is becoming more complex. Growing concerns around privacy, commercial sensitivity, cybersecurity, intellectual property, public trust, and the governance of artificial intelligence have led many organizations to restrict access to valuable datasets, contributing to what has been described as a “[data winter](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5660451)”.

This has created a paradox: just as the potential public value of non-traditional data continues to expand, access to many privately held and platform-generated datasets is becoming more constrained. Unlocking that value therefore depends not only on technological innovation but also on effective governance, [trusted stewardship](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06687), sustainable partnerships, and institutional arrangements that enable responsible data reuse.

Against this backdrop, the purpose of this report is to document how non-traditional data is already being reused in practice. Over the past two years, [we](https://opendatapolicylab.org/articles/ntd-blog-update-recent-uses-of-non-traditional-data-in-the-public-interest-january-april-2026/) [have](https://opendatapolicylab.org/articles/blog-recent-uses-of-non-traditional-data-in-the-public-interest-september-december-2025/) [periodically](https://opendatapolicylab.org/articles/new-blog-post-monitoring-the-re-use-and-impact-of-non-traditional-data/) [identified](https://opendatapolicylab.org/articles/new-blog-post-unlocking-public-value-with-non-traditional-data-recent-use-cases-and-emerging-trends/) and [highlighted](https://opendatapolicylab.org/articles/new-publications-innovating-with-non-traditional-data-recent-use-cases-for-unlocking-public-value/) emerging examples of NTD reuse from around the world. This report brings together 100 curated use cases published between late 2024 and 2026 into a single resource. The compilation does not offer a comprehensive inventory of all existing applications, but seeks to provide a representative snapshot of the current state of practice across different sectors, geographies, and data types.

The cases illustrate the remarkable diversity of both the data being reused and the public-interest questions they seek to address. They span public health, humanitarian response, climate adaptation, environmental monitoring, disaster management, mobility, labor markets, economic measurement, agriculture, digital governance, education, and urban planning, among other domains. They also demonstrate how organizations are increasingly combining non-traditional data with traditional evidence sources, machine learning techniques, and domain expertise to produce more timely, actionable, and context-specific insights.

To provide a structured overview of this rapidly evolving field, the use cases are organized into seven broad data domains: (1) digital communication and online interaction data; (2) mobility and geolocation data; (3) health and biomedical data; (4) financial and commercial data; (5) work and labor market data; (6) in-home and Internet of Things (IoT) data; and (7) environmental, geospatial, and infrastructure data. Within each domain, examples are further grouped according to more specific data types. Each use case follows a common structure, describing the public-interest challenge being addressed, the role played by non-traditional data, and why the reuse of those data matters…([More](https://docs.google.com/document/d/19ojoRQgzRZk5WNxG6m62ZHEGgelbH0pqSZaxKY5pLAU/edit?pli=1&tab=t.0))”

# 為公共利益目的再利用非傳統資料

[100 個應用案例精選彙編（2024-2026）](https://docs.google.com/document/d/19ojoRQgzRZk5WNxG6m62ZHEGgelbH0pqSZaxKY5pLAU/edit?pli=1&tab=t.0) by Stefaan Verhulst and Adam Zable：「社會快速數位化，已從根本上改變了資料樣貌。每天，人們與數位平台、行動裝置、感測器、金融系統、衛星、連網基礎設施及其他科技進行數十億次互動，產生前所未有的大量資訊，反映人類行為、經濟活動、環境變化與公共系統。這些資料通常是為了營運、商業或技術用途而產生，而非用於官方統計或研究；但若能以負責任的方式再利用，便愈來愈有機會用來處理各種公共利益挑戰。

這類所謂的非傳統資料（non-traditional data, NTD），已成為調查、人口普查、行政紀錄與官方統計等傳統證據來源的重要補充。相較於許多傳統資料集，它能提供更即時、更細緻、更連續、也更能反映行為面的資訊，讓政府、研究人員、人道組織與公民社會更能掌握快速變動的情勢，並做出更有效的回應。

從追蹤疾病爆發與人口流離失所，到監測環境惡化、估算經濟活動、改善災害應變，以及為都市規劃提供依據，NTD 正日益成為支撐公共決策之證據基礎的重要一環。

與此同時，取得與再利用非傳統資料的環境也變得更加複雜。對隱私、商業敏感性、資安、智慧財產權、公共信任，以及人工智慧治理的疑慮日增，已使許多組織開始限制對寶貴資料集的存取，進而促成了所謂的「[資料寒冬](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5660451)」。

這造成了一個弔詭現象：就在非傳統資料的潛在公共價值持續擴大的同時，許多由私人持有、平台產生的資料集，取得管道卻變得更加受限。因此，要釋放這些價值，仰賴的不只是技術創新，還包括有效的治理、[可信賴的管理機制](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06687)、可持續的合作夥伴關係，以及能促進負責任資料再利用的制度安排。

在這樣的背景下，本報告的目的，是記錄非傳統資料在實務上已如何被再利用。過去兩年來，[我們](https://opendatapolicylab.org/articles/ntd-blog-update-recent-uses-of-non-traditional-data-in-the-public-interest-january-april-2026/) [持續](https://opendatapolicylab.org/articles/blog-recent-uses-of-non-traditional-data-in-the-public-interest-september-december-2025/) [定期](https://opendatapolicylab.org/articles/new-blog-post-monitoring-the-re-use-and-impact-of-non-traditional-data/) [盤點](https://opendatapolicylab.org/articles/new-blog-post-unlocking-public-value-with-non-traditional-data-recent-use-cases-and-emerging-trends/) 並[整理重點](https://opendatapolicylab.org/articles/new-publications-innovating-with-non-traditional-data-recent-use-cases-for-unlocking-public-value/)，介紹來自世界各地新浮現的非傳統資料（NTD）再利用案例。本報告將 2024 年底至 2026 年間發表、經精選的 100 個案例彙整為單一資源。這份彙編並非要提供所有現有應用的完整清單，而是希望呈現一幅具代表性的實務現況縮影，涵蓋不同部門、地理區域與資料類型。

這些案例展現了被再利用資料的驚人多樣性，以及它們所試圖回應的公共利益議題之廣泛面向。其範圍涵蓋公共衛生、人道應變、氣候調適、環境監測、災害管理、移動性、勞動市場、經濟衡量、農業、數位治理、教育與都市規劃等領域。這些案例也顯示，各類組織愈來愈常將非傳統資料與傳統證據來源、機器學習技術及領域專業結合，以產出更即時、可行動且更貼近脈絡的洞見。

為了有系統地概覽這個快速演變中的領域，這些應用案例被整理為七大資料領域：（1）數位通訊與線上互動資料；（2）移動性與地理定位資料；（3）健康與生物醫學資料；（4）金融與商業資料；（5）工作與勞動市場資料；（6）居家與物聯網（IoT）資料；以及（7）環境、地理空間與基礎設施資料。在每個領域中，範例還會依照更具體的資料類型進一步分組。每個應用案例都遵循共同的結構，說明所要處理的公共利益挑戰、非傳統資料在其中扮演的角色，以及為何再利用這些資料很重要……([更多內容](https://docs.google.com/document/d/19ojoRQgzRZk5WNxG6m62ZHEGgelbH0pqSZaxKY5pLAU/edit?pli=1&tab=t.0))”
